provenance: I authored the Unique formalization and its additional evaluation checks, but did not author Shared or the correspondence implementation. For this cross-layer review I read all required authored units, exact Lean selections and the review-policy snapshot; I also inspected the named definitions and statement assumptions in any additionally listed source context. I compared the Shared design independently, found and requested correction of a stored-mode/path-mode wording mismatch, then reread the changed shared.steps snapshot and verified other required inputs unchanged before deciding. Listing a containing source context records the inspected definitions, not an audit of every proof tactic in that file.
rationale: unit:shared.well_formed introduces allocation, variable-rooted liveness and WF before the subsequent results. shared.state and its dependencies establish identity, storage, counter and class-table notation. Allocated is membership in object keys. Live has variable-root and initialized-field extension constructors and deliberately ignores reference mode, matching both unique and shared owning edges. Owners enumerates reference occurrences across every variable and every field; References enumerates their targets, without deduplication. WellFormed's objectKeys/variableKeys/shapes/bounds/older fields match the first three bullets. referencesComplete is an iff between occurrence membership and allocation, matching no dangling target plus at least one owner; ownersCompatible is Pairwise Compatible, allowing equal targets only when both occurrences are shared. This matches occurrence-based exclusivity and does not assert that a unique final reference alone makes an entire route unique. The older-target condition uses strict index decrease, as stated.
limitations: This comparison checks prose/notation and formal statement correspondence; it does not independently certify Lean proof checking or audit proof tactics.
